correctness.rationale: For q a prime power and d>=2q, the Krawtchouk character sum on weight-two elements is K2(t)=([d(q-1)-qt]^2-(q-2)[d(q-1)-qt]-d(q-1))/2. Averaging any feasible Fourier spectrum over one minimizing frequency-weight layer proves the sharp upper bound 1-V2/mu; g*=1-K2/mu is nonnegative, mean one, Fourier-degree two, hence attains it. Complementarity annihilates each minimum layer. The polynomial kernel argument separates h_i and nonzero-label contrasts, discards two-label and one-label terms under interior-layer swaps, and four-cycle identities force b_ij=a_i+a_j. Unless k=1+(d-2)(q-1)/q, an active-layer swap forces scalar radial rigidity; at the exceptional integral k (d congruent 2 mod q), sum a_i=0 and remaining (t-k)sum_active a_i are precisely all zero-kernel directions. Explicit subset inequalities are exactly remaining spectral nonnegativity and allow a neighborhood of 0, proving the (d-1)-dimensional polytope. Independent exact K2 calculations give (q,d,mu,mass)=(3,6,-6,11),(3,8,-8,15),(4,10,-15,28); not an unrestricted rank proof.
